items.title: Section: Closing the Causes of Obstruction — A Beginningless Loop, and the Bodhisattva Who Chooses to Return to the Dream

items.zh: 如是二種，無始世來，應知展轉更互為因。謂過去世分別為因，能生現在分別所依及所緣事。現在分別所依緣事既得生已，復能為因，生現在世由彼依緣所起分別。
items.en: These two — discrimination and its basis and object — should be understood as, since beginningless time, mutually serving as each other's cause. Past discrimination serves as cause to generate the present basis and object of discrimination. Once the present basis and object of discrimination have arisen, they in turn serve as cause, generating the present discrimination that arises resting on that very basis and object.

items.zh: 於今分別不了知故，復生當來所依緣事；彼當生故，決定當生依彼、緣彼所起分別。
items.en: Because present discrimination is not understood for what it is, it further generates the basis and object to come in the future; and because that future basis and object will certainly arise, the discrimination that arises resting on it will, just as certainly, arise as well.

items.title: Section: The Means of Purification Opens — Four Investigations, Four Kinds of True Wisdom

items.zh: 云何了知如是分別？謂由四種尋思、四種如實智故。
items.en: How is this discrimination understood for what it is? It is understood by means of four kinds of investigation and four kinds of true wisdom.

items.zh: 云何名為四種尋思？一者、名尋思，二者、事尋思，三者、自性假立尋思，四者、差別假立尋思。
items.en: What are the four kinds of investigation? The first is investigation of names; the second is investigation of things; the third is investigation of imputed self-nature; the fourth is investigation of imputed distinguishing features.

items.title: The Four Investigations Explained Through a Single Teacup

items.zh: 名尋思者，謂諸菩薩於名唯見名，是名名尋思。事尋思者，謂諸菩薩於事唯見事，是名事尋思。
items.en: Investigation of names: bodhisattvas, regarding a name, see only the name — this is called investigation of names. Investigation of things: bodhisattvas, regarding a thing, see only the thing — this is called investigation of things.

items.zh: 自性假立尋思者，謂諸菩薩於自性假立，唯見自性假立，是名自性假立尋思。差別假立尋思者，謂諸菩薩於差別假立，唯見差別假立，是名差別假立尋思。此諸菩薩於彼名、事，或離相觀、或合相觀。
items.en: Investigation of imputed self-nature: bodhisattvas, regarding an imputed self-nature, see only an imputed self-nature — this is called investigation of imputed self-nature. Investigation of imputed distinguishing features: bodhisattvas, regarding an imputed distinguishing feature, see only an imputed distinguishing feature — this is called investigation of imputed distinguishing features. These bodhisattvas, with respect to name and thing, contemplate them either separately or in combination.

items.zh: 依止名、事合相觀故，通達二種自性假立、差別假立。云何名為四如實智？一者、名尋思所引如實智，二者、事尋思所引如實智，三者、自性假立尋思所引如實智，四者、差別假立尋思所引如實智。云何名尋思所引如實智？

items.title: Section: The First True Wisdom — Name and Meaning Are Mutual Strangers, Yet Naming Still Genuinely Serves

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩於名尋思唯有名已，即於此名如實了知。謂如是名為如是義，於事假立，為令世間起想、起見、起言說故。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, having investigated names and found there to be only name, then truly understand this name for what it is: that this particular name is established for this particular meaning, imputed onto an event, in order that the world may generate conceptions, views, and speech regarding it.

items.zh: 若於一切色等想事，不假建立色等名者，無有能於色等想事起色等想；若無有想，則無有能起增益執；若無有執，則無言說。
items.en: If, with respect to every event conceived of as form and so on, the designations "form" and so on were not provisionally established, no one would be able to form the conception "form" regarding that event. And if no such conception arose, no superimposing attachment could arise. And if no such attachment arose, there would be no speech.

items.title: The Second True Wisdom — A Thing, Stripped of Its Name, Is Simply Inexpressible

items.zh: 若能如是如實了知，是名名尋思所引如實智。云何事尋思所引如實智？謂諸菩薩於事尋思唯有事已，觀見一切色等想事性離言說，不可言說。
items.en: Being able to truly understand it in this way is called the true wisdom yielded by investigating names. What is the true wisdom yielded by investigating things? Bodhisattvas, having investigated things and found there to be only the thing itself, observe that the nature of every event conceived of as form and so on is inexpressible in speech, unable to be described in words.

items.zh: 若能如是如實了知，是名事尋思所引如實智。云何自性假立尋思所引如實智？

items.title: Section: The Third True Wisdom — Imputed Nature Is Never the Thing's Own Nature, Yet Appears Exactly As If It Were

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩於自性假立尋思唯有自性假立已，如實通達了知色等想事中，所有自性假立非彼事自性，而似彼事自性顯現。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, having investigated imputed self-nature and found there to be only imputed self-nature, truly comprehend and cognize that, with respect to any event conceived of as form and so on, whatever self-nature is imputed there is never that event's own actual nature — and yet it appears exactly as if it were that event's own nature.

items.title: Section: The Eight Classical Analogies for the Dependent Nature

items.zh: 又能了知彼事自性，猶如變化、影像、嚮應、光影、水月、焰水、夢、幻相似顯現，而非彼體。
items.en: They are further able to understand that an event's own nature appears in a similar way to a magical transformation, a reflected image, an echo, a cast shadow, the moon in water, a shimmering mirage, a dream, or an illusion — appearing in this fashion, yet never being that nature itself.

items.zh: 若能如是如實了知最甚深義所行境界，是名自性假立尋思所引如實智。云何差別假立尋思所引如實智？謂諸菩薩於差別假立尋思唯有差別假立已，如實通達了知色等想事中差別假立不二之義。

items.title: The Fourth True Wisdom — Neither Existence Nor Non-Existence Applies Absolutely to Any Distinction

items.zh: 謂彼諸事非有性、非無性。可言說性不成實故，非有性；離言說性實成立故，非無性。
items.en: These events are neither existent in nature nor nonexistent in nature. Because their describable nature does not genuinely hold up, they are not existent in nature; because their inexpressible nature is genuinely established, they are not nonexistent in nature.

items.zh: 如是由勝義諦故，非有色，於中無有諸色法故；由世俗諦故，非無色。於中說有諸色法故。如有性無性、有色無色，如是有見無見等差別假立門，由如是道理，一切皆應了知。
items.en: Likewise, from the standpoint of ultimate truth, there is no form at all, since no form-phenomenon whatsoever is found within it; yet from the standpoint of conventional truth, form is not nonexistent, since form-phenomena are indeed spoken of within it. Just as with existence and non-existence, and form and formlessness, so too with visibility and invisibility and every other imputed distinguishing feature — by this same reasoning, all of it should be understood accordingly.

items.zh: 若能如是如實了知差別假立不二之義，是名差別假立尋思所引如實智。

items.title: Section: The Cost of Lacking These Four Wisdoms — Endless Wandering Through Old Age, Sickness, and Death

items.zh: 愚夫於此四如實智有所闕故，不現前故，便有八種邪分別轉，能生三事，能起一切有情世間及器世間。
items.en: Because unenlightened beings are lacking in these four kinds of true wisdom, and these do not become manifest for them, the eight kinds of mistaken discrimination therefore operate, generating the three things, and giving rise to the entire world of sentient beings and the physical world.

items.zh: 謂由如是邪分別故，起諸雜染；起雜染故，流轉生死；於生死中常流轉故，恒有無量隨逐生死種種生老病死等苦，流轉不息。
items.en: Because of this mistaken discrimination, defilement arises; because defilement arises, one cycles through birth-and-death; and because one constantly cycles through birth-and-death, immeasurable suffering — birth, old age, sickness, death, and the rest — perpetually follows along, cycling without rest.

blocks.text: How discrimination is undone: four investigations and four true wisdoms. This framework is taken up in later Yogācāra works as a stage of the path. A short passage (0490b10 area) is untranslated.

"Discrimination and its basis and object have, since beginningless time, served as each other's cause." Past discrimination produces the present object; not understood, the present discrimination produces the future one.

"Investigation of names: regarding a name, bodhisattvas see only the name. Of things: only the thing. Of imputed own-nature: only an imputed own-nature. Of imputed distinguishing features: only imputed features." They contemplate name and thing "separately and in combination".

"This particular name is established for this particular meaning, imputed onto an event, so that the world may form conceptions and speak." Without names, no conception, no clinging; but also no communication. Naming genuinely serves.
Stripped of names, "the nature of every event is inexpressible".

"Whatever own-nature is imputed is never the event's actual nature, yet it appears as if it were." Like "a magical creation, a reflection, an echo, a shadow, the moon in water, a mirage, a dream, an illusion".

"These events are neither existent in nature nor nonexistent in nature": their describable nature does not hold; their inexpressible nature is established. "From the standpoint of ultimate truth there is no form; from conventional truth, form is not nonexistent."
Beings cycle on, "birth, old age, sickness, death perpetually following along".

quiz.q: Discrimination and its basis "mutually serve as cause since beginningless time." What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use?
quiz.why: "These two … should be understood as, since beginningless time, mutually serving as each other's cause." Venerable Miào Jìng: like asking whether the chicken produces the egg or the egg the chicken — they're mutual causes.

quiz.q: Discrimination is understood "through four investigations and four true wisdoms." At what stages are these practised, per the masters?
options: Miào Jìng: investigations at heat and peak, true wisdoms at acceptance and supreme mundane; Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas on the path of preparation practice the investigations at heat and peak
quiz.why: "How is this discrimination understood for what it is? It is understood by means of four kinds of investigation and four kinds of true wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: the four investigations are at the heat and peak stages; the four true wisdoms at acceptance and supreme mundane dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: usually it's said that bodhisattvas on the path of preparation practice the four investigations at heat and peak.

quiz.q: "Investigation of names: regarding a name, seeing only the name." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: "teacup" is only the name — no teacup in it
quiz.why: "Investigation of names: bodhisattvas, regarding a name, see only the name — this is called investigation of names." Master Cháng Bǎi: "teacup" is only the name of the teacup; there's no teacup in it.

quiz.q: "Contemplating name and thing separately or in combination." How does Master Cháng Bǎi map the four investigations?
options: names and things separately; imputed nature and features in combination
quiz.why: "These bodhisattvas, with respect to name and thing, contemplate them either separately or in combination." Master Cháng Bǎi: the treatise gives four contemplations — investigating names and things is separate contemplation; investigating imputed nature and imputed features is combined contemplation.

quiz.q: The first true wisdom: names exist "so the world can conceive, view, and speak." How do the masters view name and meaning?
options: Cháng Bǎi: name and meaning are mutual guests, existing in relation; Miào Jìng: without names, people couldn't communicate
quiz.why: "This particular name is established for this particular meaning, imputed onto an event, in order that the world may generate conceptions, views, and speech regarding it." Master Cháng Bǎi: name and meaning are guests to each other, existing in mutual dependence. Venerable Miào Jìng: without names, people would have no way to communicate.

quiz.q: A thing's nature appears "like a magical creation, a reflection … a dream, an illusion." What does the magician stand for, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the magician is karma — human karma conjures a human result
quiz.why: "They are further able to understand that an event's own nature appears in a similar way to a magical transformation, a reflected image, an echo, a cast shadow, the moon in water, a shimmering mirage, a dream, or an illusion." Master Cháng Bǎi: the magician is karma; creating human karma conjures up a human result.

quiz.q: Mistaken discrimination "gives rise to defilement, and so to wandering." What three defilements does Venerable Miào Jìng name?
options: defilement of affliction, of karma, of birth
quiz.why: "Because of this mistaken discrimination, defilement arises; because defilement arises, one cycles through birth-and-death." Venerable Miào Jìng: defilement of affliction, defilement of karma, defilement of birth.
